name: Argentine Republic

places.name: Rio Grande naval air base (Super Etendard)

areaKm2.note: world_1960 Argentina polygon = ~2,769,000 km2 computed on the sphere (low); official continental area 2,780,400 km2 (mid/high). The Falkland Islands (12,173 km2) and South Georgia, occupied 2-3 April 1982, are not in the polygon and not counted; Antarctic claim excluded.

population.note: OWID (UN WPP) Argentina 1982 = 28.92M; COW NMC v7 tpop 1982 = 28,966k; World Bank SP.POP.TOTL 1982 = 28.92M; MB 1981-82 = 28,000,000 (low).

urbanization.note: OWID urban share Argentina 1982 = 83.6%. COW upop/tpop 1982 = 12,460/28,966 = 0.43 (cities over 100,000 only), not used.

activePersonnel.note: IISS Military Balance 1981-1982, Argentina entry (samlib.ru full-text transcription; data as of July 1981, the last edition before the war): total armed forces 185,500 (118,000 conscripts): army 130,000 (90,000 conscripts), navy 36,000 incl. 3,000 naval air and 10,000 marines, air force 19,500. COW NMC v7 milper 1982 = 175,000 (mid). Low: the 1962 conscript class had been released and the 1963 class was only weeks into training in April 1982; the 1962 class was recalled. Gendarmerie, coastguard and federal police (43,000) excluded.

trainedReserves.note: IISS Military Balance 1981-1982, Argentina entry (samlib.ru full-text transcription; data as of July 1981, the last edition before the war): RESERVES 250,000 (200,000 National Guard, 50,000 Territorial Guard) = recent conscript classes. Low discounts classes not recalled; high adds the 1962 class.

supportPersonnel.note: Everything outside the P roles: navy 36,000 less ~3,000 marine riflemen, air force 19,500, army armoured cavalry, artillery, 6 AD battalions, engineers, aviation, logistics, 5 corps staffs and conscripts in basic training (~85,000) = ~135,000.

mobilizationRatio.note: Active 185,500 + reserves 250,000 (MB 1981-82) = 435,500 of 28.9M = 1.5% of population on a fast call-up; a total-war mobilisation of the 18-40 male classes (CIA World Factbook 1990: 6.37M males fit for service, 1990) would reach several times that. Range 3-8%.

mobilizable.note: population x mobilizationRatio (low x low, mid x mid, high x high).

count.note: IISS Military Balance 1981-1982, Argentina entry (samlib.ru full-text transcription; data as of July 1981, the last edition before the war): 3 infantry brigades (1 mech, 2 mot, 3 regiments each) plus corps and independent infantry regiments, and the marines' 5 infantry battalions. Argentine regiments were battalion-sized (~500-800 riflemen; the 25th Regiment that landed at Stanley was ~681 men, Falklands War article). ~25-35 battalion-equivalents x ~800. Reconstruction.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5. Evidence: FN FAL, MAG, 81/120 mm mortars, Cobra and Bantam ATGW (MB 1981-82); some night sights; era-typical.

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.25-0.5. Evidence: one-year conscripts, the 1963 class barely trained; harsh field punishments and poor rations on the islands (Falklands War article). Marines (5th Bn) better (high).

count.note: IISS Military Balance 1981-1982, Argentina entry (samlib.ru full-text transcription; data as of July 1981, the last edition before the war): 3 mountain brigades, 1 jungle brigade, 1 airborne brigade, marine commando battalion; plus 601/602 army commando companies. ~16 battalion-equivalents x ~800. Reconstruction.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5. Evidence: as line infantry, plus mountain and airborne kit.

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.25-0.75. Evidence: commando companies and marines professional (high); mountain and airborne brigades conscript-based.

count.note: IISS Military Balance 1981-1982, Argentina entry (samlib.ru full-text transcription; data as of July 1981, the last edition before the war): army 200 105 mm incl. OTO Melara pack, 90 M-114 155 mm, M-59 155 mm, 20 M-7 105 mm SP, 24 Mk F3 155 mm SP, 6 M-109 = ~360 with M-59s; marines 105/155 mm (~30). Mortars excluded. Counts for M-59 and marine guns not given by MB.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5. Evidence: mostly towed 105/155 mm of 1940s-60s design.

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5. Evidence: 3rd Artillery Group fought competently at Stanley; conscript gunners.

count.note: IISS Military Balance 1981-1982, Argentina entry (samlib.ru full-text transcription; data as of July 1981, the last edition before the war): 60 M-4 Sherman, 125 TAM medium tanks, some M-41 and 120 AMX-13 light tanks = 305 + the unspecified M-41s (mid adds ~25). 120 more TAM on order.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.25-0.5. Evidence: TAM (1980 design, 105 mm gun, light armour) era-typical; Sherman and AMX-13 obsolete.

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5. Evidence: conscript crews; armoured cavalry brigades trained for the Chilean border.

count.note: IISS Military Balance 1981-1982, Argentina entry (samlib.ru full-text transcription; data as of July 1981, the last edition before the war): 300 AMX-VTP, some TAM VCTP, 75 M-3, 5 BDX, 250 M-113, 50 Mowag Roland (army) + 22 LVTP-7 and 6 Roland (marines) = ~710.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.25-0.5. Evidence: VCTP modern; AMX-VCI, M-3 half-tracks old.

count.note: IISS Military Balance 1981-1982, Argentina entry (samlib.ru full-text transcription; data as of July 1981, the last edition before the war): 1 interceptor sqn with 19 Mirage IIIEA + 2 IIIDA; 2 sqn with 26 Dagger (IAI Nesher) = 47. High allows further Daggers delivered before April 1982.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5. Evidence: Mirage III and Dagger contemporaries of the Harrier but with only R-530/Shafrir AAM and no all-aspect Sidewinder (MB lists R-530).

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.75. Evidence: skilled pilots; Daggers pressed low-level attacks on the San Carlos fleet (Falklands War article).

count.note: IISS Military Balance 1981-1982, Argentina entry (samlib.ru full-text transcription; data as of July 1981, the last edition before the war): air force 9 Canberra B-62 + 2 T-64, 68 A-4P Skyhawk, 32 MS-760A Paris, 45 IA-58A Pucara = 156; naval air 11 A-4Q; plus 5 Super Etendard delivered by April 1982 (Falklands War article: the five Etendards at Rio Grande) = 172. Low allows A-4 serviceability under the US embargo. Recce Huanquero excluded.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.25-0.5. Evidence: subsonic A-4s without ECM, Pucara COIN aircraft; only 5 Super Etendard with 5 AM39 Exocet.

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.75. Evidence: Super Etendard-Exocet sank HMS Sheffield and Atlantic Conveyor; low-level bombing sank Ardent and Antelope and hit Sir Galahad, although many bombs failed to explode (Falklands War article).

count.note: IISS Military Balance 1981-1982, Argentina entry (samlib.ru full-text transcription; data as of July 1981, the last edition before the war): army ~70 (A-109, UH-1H, Lama, CH-47C, Puma, Bell 206/212, FH-1100), air force ~60 (Hughes 500M, UH-1H, Puma, S-61R, CH-47C, Bell 212), navy ~19 (S-61D, Alouette III, Lynx, Puma) = ~150; mid discounts unserviceable airframes.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5. Evidence: mostly utility types, no dedicated attack helicopter.

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5-0.75. Evidence: army aviation sustained island garrisons until grounded by British air superiority.

count.note: IISS Military Balance 1981-1982, Argentina entry (samlib.ru full-text transcription; data as of July 1981, the last edition before the war): 1 ex-British Colossus carrier (Veinticinco de Mayo), 1 ex-US Brooklyn cruiser (General Belgrano), 9 destroyers (2 Type 42 with Exocet and Sea Dart, 3 Fletcher, 3 Sumner, 1 Gearing) = 11. Low allows Fletchers paid off before April 1982. Falklands War article: Belgrano sunk by HMS Conqueror 2 May.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.25-0.5. Evidence: 2 Type 42 modern; carrier, cruiser and 7 destroyers WWII hulls (some with Exocet refits).

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5. Evidence: professional cadre, half conscripts (18,000 of 36,000).

count.note: IISS Military Balance 1981-1982, Argentina entry (samlib.ru full-text transcription; data as of July 1981, the last edition before the war): 2-3 A-69 corvettes with Exocet (2 in MB, a third delivered 1981), 7 patrol ships, 3 large patrol craft, 2 TNC-45, 4 Dabur, 2 Higgins FAC(T), 6 Ton MCM = 26-27.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5. Evidence: A-69 corvettes modern; the rest old patrol craft.

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5. Evidence: as major ships.

count.note: IISS Military Balance 1981-1982, Argentina entry (samlib.ru full-text transcription; data as of July 1981, the last edition before the war): 2 Type 209 (Salta, San Luis), 2 ex-US Guppy (Santa Fe, Santiago del Estero). Low: Santiago del Estero was non-operational and Santa Fe was disabled at South Georgia on 25 April (Falklands War article losses list a Balao-class submarine).

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5-0.75. Evidence: Type 209 modern diesel boats; Guppies WWII-era.

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5. Evidence: San Luis was the only Argentine unit to keep operating at sea after the Belgrano sinking (Falklands War article) but scored no hits.

count.note: Batteries. IISS Military Balance 1981-1982, Argentina entry (samlib.ru full-text transcription; data as of July 1981, the last edition before the war): army 6 AD battalions (30/35/40/90 mm AA guns, Tigercat, 10 Roland SAM), marines 1 AD battalion (30 mm, 10 Tigercat); at ~3 batteries per battalion = ~21, plus air force Oerlikon/Skyguard 35 mm batteries (~4). Reconstruction from battalion counts.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5. Evidence: Roland and Skyguard-directed 35 mm modern; Tigercat and 40/90 mm guns old.

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5-0.75. Evidence: Stanley air defences kept the airfield usable through the five Black Buck raids and Harrier attacks (Falklands War article).

commandQuality.note: Rubric row: commandQuality 0.25-0.5. Evidence: junta command with no joint staff; after the Belgrano sinking the entire fleet except the submarine San Luis returned to port (Falklands War article); Veinticinco de Mayo could not launch her aircraft for lack of wind.

cohesion.note: Rubric row: cohesion 0.25-0.5. Evidence: conscript army with an officer-conscript divide and harsh punishments (Falklands War article); marine and commando units held together better.

morale.note: Rubric row: morale 0.5-0.75. Evidence: the Malvinas cause had broad popular support and lifted the junta in April 1982; conscript morale on the islands fell under cold, hunger and isolation.

weapons.note: Anchor: between 8 (1943) and 9 (1985). Evidence: AM39/MM38 Exocet, Sea Dart, Roland, Tigercat, FN FAL; but Sherman tanks and WWII naval guns (MB 1981-82).

armor.note: Anchor: 8 (rolled armour). Evidence: TAM light-armoured medium tank, AMX-13, M-4 Sherman.

ships.note: Anchor: between 8 and 9. Evidence: Type 42 destroyers with Sea Dart, Type 209 submarines; a WWII carrier and cruiser; no nuclear submarines.

fortification.note: Anchor: 8 (concrete lines). Evidence: dug-in positions on the hills around Stanley; no hardened air bases.

logistics.note: Anchor: 8 (motor transport, rail) to 9 (airlift). Evidence: 7 C-130 + 2 KC-130 tankers (MB) sustained an air bridge to Stanley; sea resupply cut by the blockade.

communications.note: Anchor: between 8 and 9. Evidence: HF/VHF radio networks; no satellite communications or tactical data links.

isr.note: Anchor: ISR 8 = radar, 9 = satellites. Evidence: SP-2H Neptune and Boeing 707 maritime reconnaissance, AN/TPS-43 radar at Stanley; no satellites.

air.note: Anchor: air 9 = 1985. Evidence: Mirage III, Dagger, Super Etendard; no AEW or modern AAM.

cyber.note: No military computer networks with attack capability before ~1985; anchor cyber 9 = 1990 networks.

gdpPerCapita.note: Maddison 2023 (OWID CSV) Argentina 1982 = 11,550 (2011 int$); 1981 = 12,125 (high), 1980 = 13,080; recession and hyperinflation.

gdp.note: population x gdpPerCapita (low x low, mid x mid, high x high), 2011 int$.

milSpendShare.note: SIPRI via OWID: Argentina 1982 = 2.70% (mid, war year), 1981 = 3.47% (high, last peacetime year, higher because the 1982 inflation wiped out the budget in real terms), 1984 = 2.16%. MB 1981-82: defence expenditure 1980 $3.38bn.

foodSurplus.note: Formula: foodSurplus = 1 - agricultural share of the labour force (share of food output not eaten by the farm population; no calorie self-sufficiency adjustment). World Bank WDI Database Archives (version 1999 Apr), SL.AGR.TOTL.ZS "Labor force in agriculture (% of total)" (ILO-based) Argentina 1982 = 12.8%. CIA World Factbook 1990: 12% (1985). Argentina was a major food exporter. Share 12.8% (range 10.0-15.0%) -> 0.872 (0.85-0.9).

annualCohort.note: World Bank 1982 (SP.POP.1519.MA.5Y, SP.POP.TOTL.MA.IN): male pop 14,247,365 x 8.39% / 5 = ~239,100 males per year. High: CIA World Factbook 1990, 277,144 males reach military age (20) annually. audit 2026-10-30: males only, the conscript-pool convention of all other snapshots (derived:cohort-from-agegroup applied to the male term only); was 473,000 for both sexes.

armor.note: Educated guess: TAM and VCTP vehicles per year from TAMSE (120 more TAM on order in MB 1981-82).

aircraft_strike.note: Educated guess: IA-58 Pucara per year from FMA Cordoba (11 on order in MB 1981-82).

roadKm.note: CIA World Factbook 1990 (Project Gutenberg #14), Argentina entry: highways 208,350 km total; 47,550 km paved (mid), 39,500 km gravel (high = paved + gravel). 1990 value; the 1982 paved network was slightly shorter (low).

railKm.note: CIA World Factbook 1990 (Project Gutenberg #14), Argentina entry: railroads 34,172 km total (1990). The 1982 network was about the same or slightly longer before 1990s closures (high).

majorPorts.note: CIA World Factbook 1990 (Project Gutenberg #14), Argentina entry lists Bahia Blanca, Buenos Aires, Necochea, Rio Gallegos, Rosario, Santa Fe; plus naval ports Puerto Belgrano, Mar del Plata, Ushuaia and Comodoro Rivadavia.

merchantTonnage.note: Educated guess: CIA World Factbook 1990 (https://www.gutenberg.org/cache/epub/14/pg14.txt): 131 ships of 1,693,540 GRT / 2,707,079 DWT in 1990 (low). The ELMA and YPF fleets were larger in 1982 before the late-1980s contraction.

supplyRangeKm.note: Educated guess: Stanley lies ~700 km from Rio Gallegos; the garrison was supplied by C-130 air bridge and, until the blockade, by sea. Mainland operations near Chile would sit on rail and road.

draftAnimals.note: Educated guess: horses (~3M) and mules in the pampas economy; mountain brigades used mule trains.

nuclearWarheads.note: FAS stockpile series (OWID) lists no Argentine warheads; the nuclear programme (Pilcaniyeu enrichment plant, announced 1983) produced no weapon.

basesAbroad.name: Puerto Argentino / Stanley (occupied Falklands, from 2 Apr 1982)

homeDefense.note: 1.1 row: familiar terrain and local supply on the mainland; high 1.2 for population support and Andean barrier against Chile. The occupied Falklands get no home bonus.

notes: Snapshot date 2 April 1982 (invasion of the Falklands); force data from IISS Military Balance 1981-82 (data July 1981; read in the samlib.ru full-text transcription at http://samlib.ru/t/temezhnikow_e_a/mb1981.shtml), cross-checked with COW NMC v7 and the Falklands War article (land forces on the islands about 10,000-13,000 at peak per the infobox; ~681 men of the 25th Regiment landed first). Personnel: active = army, navy (incl. naval air and marines) and air force incl. conscripts; National and Territorial Guard (recent conscript classes) in trainedReserves; gendarmerie, coastguard and federal police excluded. Population and territory: continental Argentina; the occupied Falklands and South Georgia are listed as bases abroad, not territory. Freedman's official history and the Military Balance 1982-83 (post-war) were not used for counts. Logistics bounds come from the 1990 CIA World Factbook and are adjusted for 1982 by judgement.
